key: Ask two questions in order: does the ulcer hurt, and what are the inguinal nodes doing? Painful ulcers are herpes with grouped vesicles and chancroid with a ragged ulcer and suppurating node; painless ulcers are syphilis with a clean chancre and rubbery nodes, LGV with a fleeting ulcer then buboes, and donovanosis with a beefy-red ulcer and no true nodes.
items: Painful grouped vesicles on a red base
hsv
Herpes simplex virus kills epithelial cells as it replicates, so clustered vesicles on an inflamed base break into shallow ulcers that expose sensory nerve endings and hurt.
Multinucleated giant cells on a Tzanck smear
hsv
Infected cells fuse into multinucleated giant cells with inclusions; the smear cannot tell herpes simplex from varicella-zoster, so lesion PCR is the more sensitive and specific test.
Latent virus in sacral ganglia that reactivates with stress
hsv
The virus travels up sensory axons and persists as an episome in the sacral dorsal root ganglia, so stress, menses or immunosuppression can trigger recurrences at the same site.
Treated with acyclovir or valacyclovir
hsv
These guanosine analogs are activated by viral thymidine kinase and stop viral DNA polymerase; they shorten outbreaks and suppress recurrences but do not eradicate latent virus.
Deep ragged ulcer with a gray purulent base
chancroid
Haemophilus ducreyi enters through microabrasions and causes a necrotic, undermined, painful ulcer with a purulent base, unlike the clean-based chancre of syphilis.
Gram-negative rods lined up like a school of fish
chancroid
H. ducreyi is a small gram-negative rod that lies in chains or parallel groups in ulcer exudate, giving the classic school-of-fish appearance on Gram stain.
Painful ulcer plus a tender unilateral node that may suppurate
chancroid
The painful ulcer is the clue that separates this from LGV: the node enlarges on one side, becomes tender, and can rupture through the skin.
Treated with a single dose of azithromycin or ceftriaxone
chancroid
One oral dose of azithromycin or one intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone treats it, in contrast with LGV and donovanosis, which need weeks of therapy.
Single painless indurated ulcer with a clean base
syph
Treponema pallidum provokes a lymphocytic and plasma cell reaction around small vessels, which produces a firm, clean-based ulcer, and the absence of pain is why it is often missed.
Spirochetes seen on darkfield microscopy
syph
T. pallidum is too thin for a Gram stain, so fluid from the chancre is examined by darkfield microscopy, which can be positive before serology turns positive.
Rubbery, painless nodes on both sides
syph
Regional nodes enlarge without acute inflammation, so they are firm, mobile and painless, unlike the painful buboes of chancroid and LGV.
Treated with benzathine penicillin G
syph
One intramuscular dose of long-acting penicillin treats primary syphilis because the spirochete stays penicillin-sensitive, and the first dose can cause a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.
Small ulcer that heals before the nodes swell
lgv
Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1 to L3 produce a tiny painless papule or ulcer that heals within days, so patients usually come in weeks later because of the nodes.
Matted painful buboes with a groove sign
lgv
The L serovars spread through lymphatics to the inguinal and femoral nodes, which swell above and below the inguinal ligament, leave a groove between them, and may drain through sinus tracts.
Treated with doxycycline for 21 days
lgv
These invasive serovars need a longer course than the 7 days that clears cervical chlamydia, so doxycycline is given for 21 days.
Proctocolitis after rectal exposure
lgv
Rectal infection with L serovars causes bloody discharge, tenesmus and pain that can mimic inflammatory bowel disease, especially in men who have sex with men.
Beefy-red ulcer that bleeds on contact
donov
Klebsiella granulomatis causes highly vascular, friable granulation tissue that bleeds easily and is painless, which sets it apart from the clean-based syphilis chancre.
Donovan bodies in macrophages
donov
A Giemsa-stained smear or biopsy shows rod-shaped organisms with a safety-pin look inside macrophages, called Donovan bodies, which are the diagnostic clue.
Subcutaneous swellings without true node enlargement
donov
Granulomatous inflammation forms subcutaneous masses in the groin, called pseudobuboes, rather than true lymphadenopathy, so enlarged nodes are not the main finding.
Treated with azithromycin for at least 3 weeks
donov
Therapy continues until the lesions have fully healed, with azithromycin for at least 3 weeks, the longest course in this group.
